score_evidence: Copy is threat/mission-framed ('harvest now, decrypt later', 'your adversaries are recording your encrypted data right now') rather than lab-metric brag, though team-pedigree brag is heavy → lab_language_intensity kept moderate-low

'Works over radio, satellite, and regular internet, even in disconnected environments' and 'From server rooms to submarines... satellite, radio, tactical edge, and standard IT, including denied and disconnected environments' — explicit DDIL/tactical-edge fluency, unusual for this stage → deployment_awareness_absence scored low
Team framed as 'Operators, cryptographers, and scientists' and CSO is a former USSOCOM CTO, but there is no CONOPS or field-feedback detail beyond team pedigree → operator_absence moderate
'no jobs data found' → hiring_profile_skew set to 10 per rule

7 employees, early-stage ('backed by' angel investors and national-security VCs, no disclosed round), SBIR/DARPA-marketplace stage rather than a fielded program, and attention split across a parallel Web3/crypto product line (tectoniclabs.xyz) → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Automatically upgrade to new security standards as they come out... even in disconnected environments' does not explain how a truly isolated node receives that upgrade
blind_spots.operator_reality: A DDIL node can be out of contact for weeks; 'automatic' upgrades still require some sync window, and the pitch never says what happens to a node that misses it — the same class of assumption that broke the 30fps crowd-detection case
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the marketing claim is meant to sound seamless; the sync-window mechanics are an engineering detail not surfaced publicly
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Your networks automatically upgrade to new security standards as they come out. Works over radio, satellite, and regular internet, even in disconnected environments.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/IL5 accreditation pathway named for crypto software claimed to run 'from server rooms to submarines'
blind_spots.operator_reality: Encryption infrastructure on a Navy platform needs an authorization to operate before it touches classified or even unclassified DoD networks; claiming submarine-to-server-room reach without naming the accreditation route is the gap that typically stalls a Navy SBIR before Phase III
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: marketing emphasizes breadth of environments, not the certification process to actually reach them
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Works Everywhere: From server rooms to submarines. Our tools operate across satellite, radio, tactical edge, and standard IT, including denied and disconnected environments.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Nearly identical homepage narrative and product framing is reused verbatim between the defense site (tectonic.xyz) and a parallel Web3/crypto site (tectoniclabs.xyz), and the team's public pedigree is dominated by crypto companies (Polygon, Hedera, TRON, Ethereum Foundation, Coinbase, Consensys) rather than defense deployment experience
blind_spots.operator_reality: A team culture built around Web3 launch cycles doesn't automatically transfer to the sustainment, training, and advocacy-chain work a Navy program needs; the defense pitch reads as a repackaging of the crypto pitch rather than a purpose-built defense product
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the same 3-person founding/eng core is running two go-to-markets, and only one team member (the CSO) has direct DoD experience
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Securing The World's Migration To Post-Quantum Encryption / Securing Web3's Migration To Post-Quantum Encryption

opener_hook: Tectonic claims automatic security-standard upgrades even in disconnected environments — what happens to a node that's been off the grid for weeks when the standard changes?
what_they_do: Post-quantum encryption infrastructure (key management, secure routing, DDIL-capable communications) marketed to both defense/national-security customers and, in parallel, Web3/blockchain projects, with a U.S. Navy SBIR award and DARPA ERIS marketplace listing.
